solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I was first to be going around shop

indicators.note: going around tells us to turn the phrase so it reads from right to left

parts.note: someone who was first led the way

explanation.surface: A boastful customer claims to have been the first person to visit the local shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I was first' gives I LED; 'going around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a kind of shop selling cooked meats and fine foods.

clue.text: Go to match perhaps when the opposition is strong

definitions.text: Go to match perhaps when the opposition is strong

parts.words: Go to match perhaps when the opposition is strong
parts.note: a match here is a marriage, and lovers who run off to marry in secret do so because their families object

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice on whether to turn up for a sports fixture against a tough team.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting reading of 'match' and 'opposition' misleads: the match is a wedding and the opposition is disapproving parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away secretly to marry is what couples do when relatives oppose the union.

clue.text: Tavern: its beer specially for spineless types

indicators.note: specially suggests the letters are prepared in a special new way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub brews a special beer aimed at weak-willed drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially' rearranges the thirteen letters of TAVERN ITS BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures with no backbone are literally spineless, like worms and insects; the word also means feeble people.

clue.text: Wild beasts in helmets

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters of the words that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: Untamed animals are wearing protective headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges BEASTS together with IN, so 'in' is part of the fodder rather than a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A basinet is a light steel medieval helmet, close-fitting and often pointed.

clue.text: Hospital event needing bed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word must be spoken, and the entry is a word sounding the same

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train

explanation.surface: Something happening at a hospital that requires a bed for the patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies are commonly delivered in hospital maternity wards, so a delivery is a typical event there.

clue.text: More like caraway cake? It's less healthy!

definitions.meaning: caraway cake is seed cake, so something with more seeds in it is jokingly more seedy
seedy means unwell or shabby, so the comparative means in poorer health

explanation.surface: A baker compares cakes and decides one full of seeds is not good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: Caraway cake is the traditional British seed cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling seedy is British slang for feeling slightly ill, so more seedy means less well.

clue.text: He gets warning about role of journalists

indicators.note: about indicates the letters are moved round into a different order

explanation.surface: A man receives a warning about the way reporters do their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of HE GETS WARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporters' core task is collecting stories and facts for publication.

clue.text: Eat long misshapen fruit

indicators.note: misshapen means put out of its proper form, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat a long, oddly shaped piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: What students of poetry will do is talk

definitions.text: What students of poetry will do
definitions.meaning: to con is to study, so students of poetry ..., a playful split
to talk is to hold a conversation with someone

explanation.surface: A teacher remarks that people studying poems will spend time discussing them.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old word for study or learn by heart, read here as CON VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to chat or exchange words in conversation.

clue.text: Victory by English? Drink!

explanation.surface: An English sporting triumph is cause to celebrate with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is a fermented grape beverage, one kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Home centre close to hospital

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A residential care centre situated near a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside is the symbolic centre of family life, so the word stands for home itself.

clue.text: Carrier bringing note up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A messenger delivering a written note upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hod is a builder's open trough on a pole for carrying bricks or mortar.

clue.text: Painter enthralling residents to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An artist whose work partly captivates the local inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' points to a run of letters inside 'enthrallING RESidents'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical artist famous for portraits.

clue.text: One irritated absurdly about nothing and getting worse

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the jumble goes round the other piece
absurdly means in a ridiculous fashion, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed over nothing finds their mood souring further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurdly' rearranges ONE IRRITATED; 'about' puts that around O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: Deterioration is the process of declining in quality or condition.

clue.text: Animal chained cruelly

indicators.note: cruelly suggests rough treatment, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A creature has been chained up in a cruel way.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: A moment in this month

definitions.meaning: inst., short for ..., is an old business-letter term for the current month

explanation.surface: Something will happen briefly at some point during the current month.
explanation.walkthrough: In old commercial letters 'the 5th inst.' meant the fifth of this month.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from Latin instans, present: a passing second, and the present month in formal correspondence.

clue.text: When a yes conceals a no

indicators.note: conceals says the words before it hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about agreement that secretly means refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'wheN A Yes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nay is an old or formal word for a negative reply or vote against.

clue.text: Maps showing street heading west to church and a river

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

explanation.surface: Maps show a street running west to a church and a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Charts are maps, especially navigational ones for sea or air.

clue.text: Silly, taking me for one that's foul

indicators.note: taking means the word accepts new letters into it
for means the new letters stand in place of the old one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is called silly for mistaking the speaker for a nasty person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking me for one' swaps the I (one) in SILLY for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foul gives off an offensive odour, as a rank or stinking thing does.

clue.text: Various notes for typist

indicators.note: various implies different arrangements, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Assorted notes are handed to a secretary to type up.
explanation.definitionFit: A steno, short for stenographer, is a shorthand typist.

clue.text: See anger that runs through France

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: Witness the fury that sweeps across the French nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' is the flow of a river, not spreading rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Change that comes with flow of water receding

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tide is the flow of the sea

explanation.surface: A shift accompanying the ebb of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise or alter it.

clue.text: Pirate getting sozzled, condition produced by pre-dinner drink

indicators.note: a sozzled person is drunk and all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A drunk pirate's state is blamed on a cocktail before supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pirate' looks like the drinker, but it is only the fodder; 'produced by' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate appetite.

clue.text: High in pitch, female voice entertains group

indicators.note: entertains means takes in as a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A high-pitched woman singer performs for a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female voice' tempts as one unit, but 'female' gives just F and the voice is separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a male singing voice pushed artificially above its normal range.

clue.text: Information about lake and valley

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Facts concerning a lake and the valley beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.
